title: Her singing, and Dr. Sushan and Eddie Watson
summary: She no longer sings because of tonsillitis but sang on a record. Russell says a doctor studied under Eddie Watson; she declines to give her birthday.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Yes, I always liked your singing and you won't sing anymore.

No, I can't sing anymore. I sang when we had a big band. I sang a lot when we were across the lake. But I have tonsillitis so I don't sing anymore. When I sing it, I start coughing. So therefore I just don't sing.
And you sang on one record then.
Yes, I sang on a record. I think it was one of Joe Moray's records. Dr. Sushan. Dr. Sushan had that session, yes.
You know, he studied under that Watson fellow. Who did? Dr. Sushan. Who did? Dr. Sushan. He did. Eddie watched the other day?
Yes. That's what he told me. I've seen his picture and all that. But you probably didn't know him.
I undoubtedly know him. I was over here then, I suppose, when he studied under Eddie. I didn't know that.
Well, that's when he was a little boy, so you wouldn't remember because he has a few years.
Well, Eddie was not that much older. Eddie, I had to be a boy too.
Well, they may have just played together as well.
Dr. Sushan. Undoubtedly, because Eddie was around his age.
Do you mind my asking, I hate to ask this question, but do you mind my asking your birthday?
I don't tell that. All right, you don't have to.
That's true. We don't want to ask that question. It just came out, because I know Dr. Sushan. I'll say this, I'm not that old.

You're not as old as Dr. Sushan. No, indeed. He never opened to me. I'm not that old. I don't consider myself an old person, which I am not that old, because I was young when I got married. I was young when I joined the band.
Fresh out of high school, you should.
